instructions.original_snippets: NEVER build the manifest from memory: the in-folder defines the scope, so a manifest without a scan misleads downstream agents.
NEVER omit the high, medium or low section of sources, even when empty: validate-manifest.sh fails and consumers cannot iterate predictably.
Do not copy files matching .env*, *credentials*, *secrets*, *token*, *.key, *.pem, *.crt, *.p12 or *.pfx into the ctx folder.
Avoid inlining a file above its threshold (1500 tokens HIGH, 2500 tokens MEDIUM): summarise it to keep the baseline within 2000 tokens.
NEVER run the skill concurrently with save-context or load-context: nothing locks the ctx folder, so the last writer wins.
After EVERY AskUserQuestion call check for blank answers: outside Plan Mode the tool can return them without showing its UI, so fall back to a numbered text list.
The in-folder is immutable bootstrap input: users drop raw documents there and no command modifies it.
Estimate tokens as words divided by 0.75 using wc -w, and delegate files above 25K tokens to the summarize-for-context sub-agent.
Write the manifest after sizing, because each action value (inline or summarized) depends on the sizing result.
Use the --force argument to rebuild an existing ctx snapshot; a plain rerun stops without changing anything.
The scanner skips a file when any path component matches a sensitive pattern, so secrets/prod.yaml is skipped by directory name.
Finish by reporting file counts and the RISEN INPUT table, then suggest /save-context baseline.
